maggie_cs: Heads-up — BlueLeaf hit onboarding friction: their server-side Node integration started returning intermittent 429s when load testing. They said errors only appear after they rolled out an ephemeral-token refresh to each serverless instance.
sam_customer: confirmed. No 401s. We call `/session/renew` on cold start per lambda, which then invokes the main `generate` path ~20x concurrently. Were on node-sdk v1.2.0, AWS Lambda in us-east-1.
indra_runtime: interesting — pattern sounds like token refresh fanout plus NAT'd IP pooling (lots of lambdas share the same NAT gateway). That amplifies per-IP concurrency. Can you paste a small trace?
sam_customer: here's a condensed log from our staging run:
```
2024-03-08T14:23:01Z func-start id=abc123
POST /v1/session/renew 200 id=abc123
for request in func: POST /v1/generate -> 429 Retry-After: 3
retry loop x3 -> eventually 200
```
We see bursts of 60 parallel generate calls from the same egress IP.
maggie_cs: thanks. Quick sanity checks: 1) are you caching tokens in an in-memory/shared cache between invocations? 2) is token TTL very short (<60s)? 3) are you pinning region or leaving routing to our geo-dns?
sam_customer: we use TTL 45s; we intentionally kept tokens short for security. Each lambda gets its own mini-cache that lives only for the duration of the container. Container reuse is low in our workload.
indra_runtime: ok that explains it. Two orthogonal contributors: 1) short TTL + container churn -> many renewals; 2) serverless NAT amplifies concurrency onto a small set of egress IPs -> route-level soft limit triggers 429s under spike.
oncall-bot: oncall pager duty ping sent to infra-team at 1729998905.
maggie_cs: propose mitigations and short-term allowances:
- short-term: request temporary burst window / quota increase for customer (we can grant for onboarding)
- application: increase token TTL to 5-10 minutes for server-side lambdas; implement a shared ephemeral-token cache (Redis/ElastiCache) or use a small central token broker to avoid per-instance renewals
- SDK: configure `sessionCache` to persist across warm starts (we can add a snippet to devex docs)
- infra: suggest adding X-Forwarded-For preservation if they sit behind customer proxy; helps us isolate per-tenant vs per-IP throttles
sam_customer: we can try increasing TTL, but are there security tradeoffs? We're okay if we use a short-lived refresh token flow with a longer access TTL for the generate calls.
indra_runtime: security note: longer access token TTL increases blast radius -> recommended pattern is a 10m access token backed by a securely stored refresh token (server process) or central broker. For serverless, shared cache is the easiest quick win.
maggie_cs: Ive opened CS internal ticket CS-7021 requesting a temporary route allowance of +500 concurrent window for 24h while BlueLeaf completes onboarding. Assigning to infra to approve.
deploy-bot: feature: node-sdk v1.2.1 scheduled to roll with `sessionCache` opt and `maxParallelRequests` param.
sam_customer: rolled TTL to 600s and wired a small ElastiCache cluster; re-ran load test and the 429s vanished under same concurrency. Latency also stabilized. Thanks everyone.
maggie_cs: perfect. Follow-ups: 1) we'll document the serverless token broker pattern in onboarding checklist; 2) devex to include a Node code snippet showing `const client = new RedwoodClient({ sessionCache: redisClient, maxParallelRequests: 16 })`
indra_runtime: filed runtime note to consider route-level telemetry that slides per-tenant thresholds vs per-route so onboards behind NAT don't get penalized as easily.
sam_customer: appreciate it :rocket: — we'll proceed to prod roll next week.
maggie_cs: closing this thread; will update internal ticket when infra approves the temporary bump.
